title: Find Factors and Multiples
objective: I can find the greatest common factor and the least common multiple of two numbers, and use each to solve a real problem.
model: listing factor pairs and multiples (hops on a number line, identical groups with nothing left over) to find the GCF and the LCM

widgets.component: Case Intake: product of 36, count by 8s, 63 ÷ 9, divides 30 evenly
widgets.root: Prerequisite fact fluency (the lesson's own warm-up is the previous lesson's content); keys 4 and 9, 32, 7, 5 recomputed.

widgets.component: Clue One: factors of 12, first four multiples of 8, GCF of 12 and 18, LCM of 4 and 6, 'GCF is 36 because 36 is in both times tables'
widgets.root: Recomputed all; the err card (a common multiple instead of a common factor) is the factor/multiple confusion at Step 3.

The 'Factors' cell is a free-text list graded by exact string equality ('1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36'): '1,2,3,4,6,9,12,18,36', '1 2 3 4 6 9 12 18 36' or a different order are marked wrong, on an input with inputmode=decimal.
widgets.replacement: Replace the typed list with 9 toggle chips (1…36, only divisors of 36 are correct) so the student selects the factors, then keep the numeric GCF cell (12). If a text cell remains, split on commas/spaces and compare as a sorted set in K.tbl.

widgets.component: Using prime factors, 48 = 2×2×2×2×3 and 36 = 2×2×3×3. What is their GCF?
widgets.root: Reads the GCF off a prime factorization ('12, from the shared 2 × 2 × 3'); prime factorization and factor trees are the content of 6-13, and 6-12 teaches the prime-factor method for LCM.
widgets.replacement: Replace with a list-method item: 'The factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48 and of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Which numbers are common factors? What is the greatest?' (key 12 with named wrong choices: 'the last factor of 36', 'the product 144', '6').

widgets.component: Ayasha's painting every 8 weeks and pottery every 6 weeks: when next together, and the 'GCF is 2' error
widgets.root: Recomputed 24 weeks (LCM) and 2 weeks (GCF applied to a schedule); the err card is the lesson's key 'which tool' misconception.

widgets.component: Generated factor or multiple, common factors list, 'greatest number of bracelets' stories, number of factors and common factors
widgets.root: Checked 70-80 draws per level: GCF stories (8 for 24 and 32, 15 for 75 and 120), factor counts (72 → 12) and common-factor counts (96 and 120 → 8) are exact.

widgets.component: Hops: a frog hops from 0 to a flag; tap every hop size that lands exactly on it
widgets.root: A real number-line manipulative for factors (35 → 1, 5, 7, 35); no timer, tap-to-hop; the same activity at L3 and 'multiples' L4 in the challenge studio covers common multiples.

widgets.component: Verdict: GCF of 48 and 36, LCM of 6 and 8, which tool for repeating schedules, supply runs, common but not greatest factor, factors of 45
widgets.root: Self-contained and right (12, 24, LCM, week 24, 3, 6); the five choices for 5.5 isolate 'common but not greatest'.

widgets.where: Challenge §1 items 1.1-1.4, 1.6 (gen:gcfFind L2, L3; factorsMultiples L2-L4)
widgets.component: Identical bracelets/rows, three-number GCF, multiple of 10, common factors, 'I am a factor of 84, a multiple of 21, odd'
'You want to write 15 + 9 as a product: (a number) × (a sum). What is the greatest number you can factor out?'
widgets.root: 98 of 400 L4 draws (24%) are factoring a sum, a(b + c), the distributive property of 6-14 ('The GCF of 49 and another number is 7' and 'pair with GCF 1' draws are right).
widgets.replacement: Replace the factor-out subtype with 'Two ribbons are 42 cm and 63 cm. What is the longest piece that cuts both with nothing left over?' (21) and 'Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 7?' (choices 14 and 21 ...).

widgets.component: Case Files: LCM error card, GCF/LCM table, 54 cards and 72 prints, square stickers on a 60 × 45 cm board (figure), vault code, 24 red and 96 blue tags
widgets.root: Rendered the board figure (a proportional 60 cm × 45 cm rectangle, labels 60 cm and 45 cm) and recomputed 3 cards per folder, 12 stickers (15 cm squares: 4 × 3), code 20 (multiple of 5, 6 factors), 24 bundles; the table cells (6, 36, 2, 20) are numeric.

widgets.where: Challenge §3 items 3.1-3.3 (act:hops factors L3, multiples L4; sort)
widgets.component: Forensics Lab: two flags / two hoppers up to 84, sort 8, 12, 48, 72, 18, 30 as factor, multiple or neither of 24
widgets.root: Hops L4 asks to tap every number where both hoppers land (all common multiples, not only the first); sort recomputed (8, 12 | 48, 72 | 18, 30).

widgets.component: Alibi Detective: factors of 36 left incomplete, GCF taken as the largest listed number, guards' 3-day return, '5 is a multiple of 20'
widgets.root: Each error at the right step (Step 3, Step 3, Step 1); 4.3 shows why a schedule problem is LCM not GCF.

widgets.component: Mastermind Boss: all factors of 28, GCF of 36 and 90, multiple of 4 and factor of 36, which problem is GCF, 12th multiple of 7
Hot dogs and buns for 24 guests; create two Case Files problems with the same numbers
widgets.root: Pass on 40 characters and self-ticked rubric lines; 2.2 has an empty keyword list and its stem never says how many of each he must have at least, so the written answer is not checkable.
widgets.replacement: Rewrite 2.2 as: 'Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. What is the smallest number of each he can buy so he has the same number of hot dogs and buns?' with two numeric boxes (4 packs of hot dogs, 5 packs of buns) graded by value, then a one-line reason chosen among three.
